title: GET /api/reference answers with the product's reference as JSON
statement: The response MUST be 200 with `content-type: application/json` and the `Reference` that `buildReference` builds for the product root, its own kinds and checks included.

title: POST /api/write answers the changed rows, or the refusal with its reasons
statement: A write the store accepts MUST answer 200 with `ok: true`, the tables and files it changed and each changed row before and after; a write the store refuses MUST answer 422 with `ok: false`, a sentence and every store problem with its command index, and MUST change no file.

title: POST /api/write refuses what is not a write from the app
statement: The endpoint MUST answer 405 to any method but POST, 403 to a request from another site, 415 to a body that is not `application/json`, 413 to a body over 1 MB, and 400 to a body that is not `{ commands }` with 1 to 500 commands of a known shape, each with a sentence and no write.

title: POST /api/write writes to the folder of the product its commands name
statement: A write MUST be applied in the data folder of the product whose records (or whose ID's prefix) its commands name, and one that names none to the workspace's own. A write naming records of two products MUST answer 422 with the reason and change no file.

title: GET /api/history reads git safely for the record's own rows
statement: The endpoint MUST find the data file that holds the record's row from the data by the record's ID and MUST answer 404 (`no-record`) for an ID no record has, never reading a path from the request. It MUST answer 400 for a missing ID, a negative `skip`, or a `commit` that is not a hex hash of 4 to 40 characters or `working`. It MUST run git with argument arrays, never through a shell, inside the product root, with no optional locks or prompts, stopped after a time limit and cut at an output cap (the answer says `truncated`). The list MUST hold the commits that changed the record's rows, newest first, twenty a page with `more`, and the changes the working tree holds that are not committed yet. A folder that is not a git repository, or a machine without git, MUST answer 200 with `no-repo` and a calm message. Answers carry `cache-control: no-store`.

title: A record's history is read from git, never written
statement: A record's history MUST come from git's own log of the record's rows in its table's data file, the file found from the data by the record's ID, never from a path a request names. Reading it MUST change nothing: no commit, no lock, no change to the git config, and no command built from text a shell reads.

title: GET /api/baseline reads a product's rows at a commit from git, never writing
statement: The endpoint MUST answer 400 for a missing product or a `since` that is not `commit`, `branch` or a full commit hash, and 404 for a product no folder holds. It MUST read the product folder's data files at the commit asked for from git, run with argument arrays, never through a shell, inside the product root, stopped after a time limit, and MUST change nothing. A folder outside any git repository, or a machine without git, MUST answer 200 with `no-repo`, and a repository with no commits or no default branch 200 with `no-commit`, each with a calm message. Answers carry `cache-control: no-store`.

title: GET /api/spec answers with the workspace's data, or 500 with the reason
statement: The response MUST be 200 with the schema description, each product folder's stored rows as its data files hold them, and the checks' problems and coverage, and MUST NOT be cached. When the data cannot be loaded, the response MUST be 500 with the reason, so the page says what is wrong rather than showing other data.

title: GET /api/spec serves every product of the workspace, each from its own folder
statement: The response MUST hold every product the workspace shows: one schema for them all, and each product folder's rows apart, with its data folder from the workspace root, the workspace's own first; and every product's problems, recorded exceptions and coverage, each worked out in its own folder. One product ID in two folders MUST answer 500 with the reason.

title: GET /api/events streams spec:changed until the page closes it
statement: GET /api/events MUST answer 200 with a `text/event-stream` that is not cached, start with a `: connected` comment, send `data: spec:changed` whenever the product's data files or Lathe's own checks or schema change, and stay open until the client closes it.
